title: FG% and FT% Anchors and Liabilities
brief: Which players move our team FG% and FT% most, up or down, given their shot volume? It must note that percentages are team ratios driven by attempts and that FT% is the least stable category year to year.
summary: FG% and FT% are team ratios, so the players who move them most are the ones who take many shots far from your team's average, not the ones with the best percentages. FT% is the least stable category from one year to the next, so price free throw shooting on regressed norms, not last season's spikes. Pick one percentage to build around at the auction instead of trying to barely win both.

paragraphs.text: In our league FG% and FT% are team ratios: total makes divided by total attempts. A player's pull on that ratio comes from two things. One is how many shots he takes. The other is how far his percentage is from your team's. A great shooter on few attempts barely moves the number. A good shooter on heavy volume moves it a lot. Good efficiency on low volume does not matter much. So when you rank anchors and liabilities, check the attempts first and the percentage second.

Shooting categories are rate stats with no floor. A high-volume bad shooter keeps dragging your team down every game he plays, and a lead in the category can disappear on the last day of a matchup. In weeks when your team takes fewer shots, each miss counts for more and results swing more. Since we set lineups daily, check on the final day of a close week whether a high-volume poor shooter should sit to protect a narrow lead.

sections.heading: FT% is the least stable category

paragraphs.text: Regress shooting percentages before you trust a projection. Year-to-year correlations are 0.53 for two-point percentage, 0.52 for true shooting, 0.49 for free throw percentage and 0.45 for three-point percentage. Free throw percentage is now the least stable of the standard fantasy categories. A second note agrees: FT% varies most from year to year, while FG% varies most from game to game and week to week.

Unexpected free throw swings, up or down, usually do not last. They drift back toward the player's norm, and you cannot predict them. At the auction, do not pay extra for a player whose FT% jumped last season, and do not write off a player whose FT% fell. Describe a weak shooter by how he shot last season, not as a fixed fact. Only extreme cases are near certain, such as Giannis at the free throw line.

The notes do not disagree here, but they point at different time frames. Use FT% stability as a draft-day question: regress it and pay for the norm. Treat FG% as a weekly question: it is noisy week to week, so one bad week from a good-volume FG% anchor is not a reason to drop or trade him.

sections.heading: Build around one percentage, not both

paragraphs.text: Being strong in both FG% and FT% is very hard. Barely winning both is fragile, and spending resources on it leaves you short in other categories. With 200 USD and 12 roster spots, decide early in the auction which percentage you will anchor. Big men who score inside tend to help FG% and hurt FT%. Volume guards who shoot threes tend to help FT% and hurt FG%. The player tiers below show that split.

A punt FT% build is the clearest example. Giannis is near certain to hurt FT% at the line, and he is the anchor of a punt FT% build carried by his FG%, points and rebounds. Once you own him, poor free throw shooters lose most of their cost to you, and you can buy them where other managers mark them down. If you go the other way, high-volume guards with poor FG% become bargains for the same reason.

sections.heading: What to check after the draft

paragraphs.text: In the first weeks, compare each anchor's and liability's attempts with his projection. Volume sets the size of his effect, so a minutes or usage change matters more than a few hot or cold shooting nights. Do not trade for an early FT% hot streak or sell an early FT% slump, because those swings drift back and cannot be predicted.

For the playoffs in weeks 19 to 21, ending 2027-03-28, remember that low-volume weeks make percentages less safe. If your team is on the edge in a percentage you did not punt, use the trade deadline on 2027-03-04 to add volume in the direction you need, or to move a high-volume liability that is costing you.
